summary: setup.py contains auto-execution harness for a missing setup.sh
details: saeka 1.0.0's setup.py defines execute_deployer(), called at module top-level during pip install, which chmods a sibling setup.sh to 0755 and invokes it via bash under a comment labeled 'AUTO-EXECUTION ENGINE... runs immediately when pip install saeka'. The published sdist does not include setup.sh, so nothing executes on install of this artifact. The rest of the package is stub/placeholder content (empty README '# itzpy', no py_modules or real code). No network I/O, no credential reads, no exfiltration, and no attacker-controlled payload are present in the shipped bytes; the mechanism is a dropper-shaped scaffold in which any future release adding setup.sh would gain arbitrary install-time execution on installers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
